| [THEORY-078](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-078.md) v2 | Top Fisher eigenvalues span the class means | Papyan (2019), [LIT-619](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-619.md): for softmax cross-entropy the Gauss–Newton matrix G, which is the model's Fisher averaged over inputs, is an uncentred second moment of logit derivatives indexed by class and logit. It decomposes exactly into four terms (Eq. 28), and its top C eigenvalues match those of the class-mean term G₁. Papyan (2020), [LIT-613](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-613.md), splits those C into one global-mean outlier and C − 1 between-class ones, finds a C(C − 1) cross-class mini-bulk beneath them, and proves the whole pattern for a Gaussian toy model. Papyan (2018), [LIT-617](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-617.md), supplies the measurements and the attribution of the Hessian's outliers to G. The decomposition is algebra. That G₁ carries the outliers is measured, by eye, under a training protocol narrower than practice. So this is Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-080](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-080.md) v4 | NTK eigenvalues schedule the Occam penalty | The filer's synthesis, stated by no source. Its exact half is filed as the record's own claim, CLAIM-384; what stays here is the spherical account. A network linearised at initialisation, with an isotropic Gaussian prior on its parameters and Gaussian noise, is MacKay's linear-in-parameters model ([LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md)). Its Occam factor is −½ Σ log(1 + βλ_a/α) over the eigenvalues of JᵀJ. These are the empirical NTK's, which on uniform spherical data form Bietti & Bach's degree blocks, nµ_k with multiplicity N(d, k) ([LIT-608](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-608.md)). Degrees whose βnµ_k exceeds α pay about ½ log n per harmonic, and degrees below pay almost nothing. With µ_k ~ k^(−d), the number of paid directions γ grows as n^((d−1)/d), not as the parameter count. Basri et al.'s bound ([LIT-612](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-612.md), Eq. 14) is the matching data-fit term. The kernel's decay exponent is the schedule of the penalty. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-082](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-082.md) | Natural-gradient efficiency needs full-rank Fisher | Amari (1998), [LIT-607](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-607.md). Theorem 1 is a Lagrangian derivation: under \|dw\|² = Σg_ij dw_i dw_j the steepest-descent direction is −G⁻¹∇L, so it changes with G. Theorem 2 shows that online learning with step 1/t along the Fisher natural gradient attains the Cramér–Rao bound G⁻¹/t, and its proof uses G(w*)⁻¹. Watanabe, [LIT-616](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-616.md), Eq. 14, calls a truth regular when the optimum is one point and its Fisher is positive definite, and singular otherwise. From Amari's own Eq. 6.12, the score for hidden unit i's input weights carries the factor v_i. So the Fisher of a multilayer perceptron loses rank wherever an output weight is zero. That set is part of the optimum whenever the teacher needs fewer hidden units than the student has. Active because each step is checkable in the two texts. The claim that the Fisher is the only invariant metric is Chentsov's, cited and not held. | Active |
| [THEORY-083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md) v4 | Neural collapse forms, only partly on ImageNet | Papyan, Han & Donoho (2020), [LIT-618](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-618.md), measured 480 trained classifiers on seven datasets with VGG, ResNet and DenseNet. Through the terminal phase, within-class variability of last-layer features falls (NC1), and the centred class means become equinorm and equiangular with cosine −1/(C − 1) (NC2). The classifier aligns with them (NC3), and the decision becomes nearest class mean (NC4). They prove that NC1 and NC2 imply NC3 and NC4 for the MSE-optimal and max-margin classifiers, and that the simplex ETF is the unique error-exponent-optimal codebook. Read from the plots, collapse is close to complete on the four easier datasets and partial on ImageNet at the last epoch. Papyan (2020), [LIT-613](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-613.md), sees class means separate and grow more orthogonal with depth. The measurements cover one protocol, and the dynamics are unexplained outside free-features models. Within them, THEORY-278 (LIT-974) derives collapse for MSE under a re-whitened flow, and THEORY-286 (LIT-994) gives the cross-entropy endpoint under class imbalance. The paper's further claim, that the Hessian's class outliers are a symptom of collapse, is argued and not measured, and is left to [THEORY-078](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-078.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md) v4 | Lazy Fisher inherits NTK harmonic blocks | The filer's synthesis, stated by no source. The identity is linear algebra: JᵀJ (parameters × parameters) and JJᵀ (samples × samples) have the same non-zero eigenvalues. Under squared loss JᵀJ is the Gauss–Newton matrix and the Fisher. JJᵀ is the empirical NTK Gram matrix, which in the kernel regime on uniform spherical data has the degree-block spectrum of Bietti & Bach (2021), [LIT-608](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-608.md): µ_k with multiplicity N(d, k). The threshold claim draws on Cao et al. (2019), [LIT-624](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-624.md). Their guarantees are stated only for whole eigenspaces, with sample costs that grow as the gap below them shrinks. It also draws on Basri et al. (2019), [LIT-612](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-612.md), where a structural zero block shows up in a finite sample as small non-zero eigenvalues. No paper filed computes a Fisher spectrum in this regime. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-085](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-085.md) v2 | K-FAC misplaces cross-class Fisher pairings | Papyan (2020), [LIT-613](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-613.md): per layer, the Fisher is a weighted sum of Kronecker products of features and backpropagated errors (Eq. 7.5), and its class outliers come from class means of gradients that are approximately h_c ⊗ δ_c. K-FAC (Martens & Grosse 2015, [LIT-622](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-622.md)) multiplies the class-averaged feature covariance by the class-averaged error covariance. Papyan finds its outliers and mini-bulks "drastically misaligned", and the class-wise CFAC aligns much better at deep layers. The identity relating the two, CFAC − K-FAC = the class-weighted between-class covariance of the factors, is the record's own and is filed as CLAIM-391. The evidence for the mechanism is one MLP, spectra only, judged by eye. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-086](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-086.md) v2 | NTK fits eigenspaces at eigenvalue-set rates | Three derived results that compose. Cao et al. (2019), [LIT-624](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-624.md), Theorem 4.2: for a wide two-layer ReLU network, the training residual's component in the top-r_k NTK eigenspace falls as (1 − λ_{r_k})^T, for any target. Basri et al. (2019), [LIT-612](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-612.md): on uniform spherical data the Gram matrix is a convolution, so its eigenvectors are harmonics, with closed-form eigenvalues per frequency. The bias-free kernel is zero on odd frequencies k ≥ 3, and a bias restores them. Bietti & Bach (2021), [LIT-608](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-608.md), Corollary 3: the L-layer ReLU NTK decays as k^(−d) on S^(d−1), the same exponent at every depth. Active for the kernel regime on uniform spherical data, where every step is proved. It says nothing about networks whose kernel moves. | Active |
| [THEORY-087](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md) v4 | Singular models pay λ log n, below d/2 | MacKay (1992), [LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md), writes the evidence as best-fit likelihood times an Occam factor, the ratio of posterior to prior accessible volume, which under a Gaussian approximation is P(w_MP)(2π)^{k/2} det^{-1/2}A. When the likelihood dominates, det A grows as n^d, so the penalty is (d/2) log n. Watanabe's WBIC paper, [LIT-616](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-616.md), recovers that case (Lemma 3, Theorem 5) and states what replaces it when the Fisher information is degenerate at the optimum: λ log n − (m − 1) log log n, with λ the RLCT (Theorem 2). The regular half is re-derived by Laplace's method with its conditions. The singular half is Watanabe's cited theorem, checked by exact free energies in two singular models of known λ. The volume reading of λ is in Watanabe's book, which is unread. | Active |
| [THEORY-092](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-092.md) v3 | Behavioural capacity doesn't fix intelligence | Block (1981), [LIT-642](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-642.md): the strongest behaviourist conception of intelligence, a capacity to give sensible responses to any sequence of inputs, "whatever they may be", is met by a machine that stores every sensible conversation of a test's length and looks up its next reply, yet "the machine has the intelligence of a toaster". So psychologism is true: two systems alike in all actual and counterfactual behaviour can differ in intelligence through the processing that mediates it. Block (1995), [LIT-630](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-630.md), n. 1: the same machine refutes the wider claim that there is no mental difference without a behavioural one. It is a claim about constitution, not evidence: performance stays evidence for competence. It names no required kind of processing, and its machine is a lookup table, not a trained network. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-104](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-104.md) v2 | Best OOD readout layer lies below the top | Uselis & Oh (2025), [LIT-678](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-678.md): linear probes on frozen intermediate layers of image classifiers beat last-layer retraining under shift, with zero-shot worst-group accuracy 79.4 → 87.1 (Waterbirds) and 56.0 → 82.0 (CelebA), layer 7 of 8 beating layer 8 on every subpopulation dataset, while in-distribution accuracy is best at the last layer. Chang, Deng & Chen (2025), [LIT-657](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-657.md): in GPT-2 Small on a synthetic task, early-exit out-of-distribution accuracy peaks at layer 10 (56.90%) and falls to 50.00% at layer 12 while in-distribution accuracy climbs to 93.17%. The layer is chosen on out-of-distribution data throughout; ViT gains are small; the language-model evidence is one synthetic task; and Chang et al.'s information estimate is questioned in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-105](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-105.md) v2 | Fine-tuned hull points beat their own members | Gueta et al. (2023), [LIT-658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-658.md): RoBERTa-base models fine-tuned on the same dataset, the same task family, or any of 12 GLUE and SuperGLUE datasets cluster in weight space. Sampled points in the convex hull of each group beat the group's own members in 88% to 96.7% of comparisons. Extrapolating past the members raises the loss quickly, so the members sit near the region's edge and averaging moves inward. The paper calls the region convex, but shows only that the hull lies inside it, by a probe-based loss. Its reading of model soups and SWA as picking points inside the region is argued in its §8, not tested. Moving from the centroid towards the origin stays low-loss far past the members, which the authors cannot explain. Promoted 2026-10-20 on the probe-loss comparisons measured (ADR-047 v3); the geometric thesis is THEORY-828. | Active |
| [THEORY-106](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-106.md) | Ridge removes the double-descent peak | Liao, Couillet & Mahoney (2020), [LIT-679](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-679.md): for random Fourier features with n, p and N large together, the test MSE has a closed form through a deterministic equivalent of the resolvent. As λ → 0 its corrections jump from O(1) to order 1/λ across 2N = n, det(Ω⁻¹) scales as λ, and the test error diverges at 2N = n unless the test data lie within about λ of the training data. At λ = 10⁻⁷ and 10⁻³ the curve has a singular peak; at the tuned λ ≈ 0.2 and at 10 it has none. Dereziński, Liang & Mahoney (2019), [LIT-683](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-683.md): exact MSE of the minimum-norm estimator under a surrogate design, peaking at n = d with value σ² tr(Σ⁻¹), and below the threshold equal in expectation to ridge regression at the λn that makes the ridge effective dimension n. Proportional-limit theorems for one shallow model each; nothing here reaches trained deep networks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-107.md) | Merging loses accuracy through interference | Yadav et al. (2023), [LIT-675](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-675.md): keeping only the top 20% of each task vector by magnitude loses almost nothing, so most of an update is redundant. Among the entries that remain, signs conflict between models, more so as more models are merged. Merging (IA)³ models with the multitask model's signs reaches 72.0 against 73.1 for multitask training and 66.4 for TIES with elected signs. That is the strongest evidence that sign is the bottleneck. But the oracle signs come from training on every task's data, the ablation finds rescaling and the disjoint mean matter more than election, and conflicts are as frequent among checkpoints of one task as across tasks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-108](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-108.md) | Connectivity, not flatness, predicts accuracy | Yang, Hodgkinson, Theisen, Zou, Gonzalez, Ramchandran & Mahoney (2021), [LIT-663](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-663.md): thousands of trained networks on a load by temperature grid, measured by the endpoint Hessian, by mode connectivity on a trained Bezier curve between two independent runs, and by CKA of their outputs. Phases III (flat, poorly connected) and IV-A (flat, connected) have almost the same Hessian and different accuracy; with 10% noisy labels the sharp, unconverged phases beat phase III; label noise barely moves the Hessian while connectivity and CKA fall. The best accuracy is in the flat, connected, high-similarity phase IV-B. The counterexamples are to the anthology's [ANTH-SOTA-012](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/practices.d/SOTA-012.md). One architecture family carries most of it, phases are read by eye, and connectivity alone also fails when the load is data amount. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-109](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-109.md) v2 | SGD solutions form one connected low-loss set | Garipov et al. (2018), [LIT-673](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-673.md), and Draxler et al. (2018), [LIT-653](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-653.md), found independently that minima of deep networks trained from different initializations are joined by paths of near-constant loss, a one-bend curve or an AutoNEB path, while the straight line between them climbs to near-chance error. Benton et al. (2021), [LIT-656](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-656.md), widened curves to simplicial complexes joining up to seven modes and a low-loss region of at least 10 dimensions. Kuditipudi et al. (2019), [LIT-671](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-671.md), proved that dropout-stable solutions are always joined, and constructed global minima that are not, so connectivity belongs to found solutions. Proposed: the evidence is pairs and small complexes of CIFAR classifiers. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-110](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-110.md) v2 | Solution sets are star domains | Sonthalia et al. (2024), [LIT-659](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-659.md), conjecture that below the width at which SGD solutions become convex modulo permutation they are still a star domain, and train a star model whose barriers to held-out solutions, after weight matching, are about 2–5 times lower than those between solutions (ResNet-18 CIFAR-10 0.078 against 0.383; ImageNet 2.794 against 5.948), and not zero. Lin et al. (2024), [LIT-682](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-682.md), prove star-shaped linear connectivity for wide two-layer teacher–student and deep linear networks, and find centres for five trained image classifiers with no permutation. Proposed: reduced, not zero, and no held-out test without alignment. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md) v4 | Linear connectivity implies feature linearity | Zhou et al. (2023), [LIT-674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-674.md): whenever two image classifiers are linearly mode connected, by spawning or by permutation, the features of nearly every layer of the interpolated network are proportional to the interpolation of the endpoints' features. This is layerwise linear feature connectivity, and two conditions, weak additivity of ReLU and a commutativity of weights with features, imply it exactly. Lubana et al.'s Lemma 2, [LIT-669](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-669.md), gives the exact one-hidden-layer case: linear connectivity between interpolating minima forces shared activation patterns, and with shared patterns the hidden features are linear along the path. Measured on pairs at three interpolation points, image classification only. The regularity outside image classification, and the step to many-model averages such as soups and SWA, are QUESTION-318. | Active |
| [THEORY-112](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-112.md) v4 | Symmetry alignment removes barriers with width | Entezari et al. (2022), [LIT-652](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-652.md), conjectured that SGD solutions are one basin modulo permutation. Git Re-Basin (2023), [LIT-661](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-661.md), aligned MNIST MLPs and 32×-wide ResNet-20s to zero barrier, but not 1×-width models or ImageNet ResNet-50. Ferbach et al. (2024), [LIT-680](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-680.md), proved it for wide nets with independent neurons, with a width requirement exponential in the previous layer's width. Theus et al. (2025), [LIT-664](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-664.md), took transformers to zero only with an orthogonal map on the residual stream added; permutations alone left 0.29–1.60. Bo Zhao et al. (2025), [LIT-655](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-655.md), place permutations inside the full symmetry group. Lubana et al.'s barriers between models that compute differently are the boundary. Whether most of the barrier goes at standard width on ImageNet or a language corpus under data-free alignment, and whether the barrier left rises with depth, is QUESTION-317. | Active |
| [THEORY-113](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-113.md) v2 | Merging disjoint-task ResNets trails the ensemble | Stoica et al. (2023), [LIT-665](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-665.md), merge ResNets trained from different initialisations on disjoint label sets. Permute-then-average fails, which they explain by the permuted model lying in a basin for its own task only. Mean cross-model feature correlation falls with depth (0.50, 0.37, 0.27 at three depths). Merging only the early layers and keeping later layers as task heads recovers most of the ensemble's accuracy. Merging features within one model as well as across both helps once the models are wide enough to hold redundant features. With full merging on ImageNet-1k, ZipIt! is no better than permutation (8.6%). No same-task control separates the effect of task difference from that of depth; that is QUESTION-316. | Active |

| [THEORY-115](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-115.md) v3 | Shared-start connectivity needs shared objectives | Mirzadeh et al. (2020), [LIT-651](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-651.md): from a task-1 solution, a model trained on tasks 1 and 2 together stays on a low task-1 loss line from the start, and one trained on task 2 alone does not. Adding noise to task 2's inputs, corrupting its labels, or removing classes separates the solutions progressively. The authors explain it by curvature: the multitask direction avoids the earlier task's top Hessian eigenvectors. Gueta et al. (2023), [LIT-658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-658.md): fine-tuning runs from one pretrained model are linearly connected within a dataset and a task family. Wen et al. (2023), [LIT-681](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-681.md): in class-incremental learning the line between adjacent continual minima crosses a ridge in the old tasks' loss. Limits: much of the measured breakage is forgetting at the endpoint, not a barrier, and FedAvg models from one random start under one global objective are separated by a barrier that grows with heterogeneity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-116](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-116.md) v2 | Surviving barriers mark different mechanisms | Lubana et al. (2022), [LIT-669](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-669.md): models that rely on a synthetic cue and models that ignore it are separated by a linear barrier even after permutation matching. Fine-tuned models that keep a linear path to their parent keep its cue, and those that lose the path lose the cue. Their Conjecture 1 states this claim's direction. What their Appendix F.3 proves, for a one-hidden-layer ReLU network with interpolating minima, is the converse: linear connectivity forces identical activation patterns, so models relying on attributes of different complexity cannot be linearly connected under any permutation. Zhou et al. (2023), [LIT-674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-674.md), support that converse in deep image classifiers, where linearly connected pairs have features that blend layer by layer. The stated direction rests on experiments with synthetic cues and on a one-layer sufficiency argument. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-117](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-117.md) v4 | Pair coverage, not data volume, drives composition | Uselis, Dittadi & Oh (2025), [LIT-667](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-667.md). In an n × n grid of two concepts with k combinations seen per value, ResNet-50s trained from scratch fit seen pairs and fail on unseen ones; four times the data of the same combinations leaves 60–80% drops, while more values and more combinations help. Features pass from spurious, to decodable but entangled, to linearly factored as coverage grows. Model selection was on the test set, by design, so the results bound what is possible. The record re-derived that exactly factored embeddings of every unseen pair are fixed by seen pairs connecting every value, as the paper's k = 2 cycle does. Honest selection, other architectures and more concepts are [QUESTION-207](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-207.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-175](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-175.md) v4 | Relative representations transfer only roughly | Moschella et al. (2022; ICLR 2023), [LIT-849](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-849.md), as read in [NOTE-652](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-652.md). The invariance is by construction; its class (the maps preserving each sample's cosines to the anchors, which include every orthogonal map times a positive scalar and every per-sample positive rescaling, but not translations) is the reader's statement, re-derived in a dated note. The approximate agreement is the paper's evidence: relative vectors match at cosine 0.86–0.97 across encoders, while ten-nearest-neighbour overlap is 0.10–0.39. It does not say the maps between trained spaces are isometries, which the source never measures ([QUESTION-211](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-211.md)), nor that the transfer needs no paired data: the anchors are paired data. | Active |

| [THEORY-181](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-181.md) v4 | Addition generalises when pairs pin translation | Liu et al. (2022), [LIT-858](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-858.md), in a toy built for it: same-answer training pairs force equal embedding sums, equal sums carry answers to unseen pairs, and for addition with p = 10 the fraction at which the forced equations first pin the embedding to a + kb (about 0.4) matches the onset of generalisation and Power et al.'s critical fraction ([LIT-341](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-341.md)). | [THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md) v2 | Converged SGD samples a modified Gibbs law | Kunin et al. (2021), [LIT-1011](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1011.md), read in [NOTE-711](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-711.md). Modelled as an underdamped Langevin equation with noise covariance proportional to the Hessian, SGD at the end of training converges to a nonequilibrium stationary state: Gibbs on a modified loss whose curvature undoes the Hessian's anisotropy, with inverse temperature S(1 − β²), in broken detailed balance. A ResNet-18 on ImageNet explores isotropically in a plane where the loss is anisotropic, oscillates at Hessian-dependent rates, and moves at the predicted speed across a hyperparameter sweep. For the learned-structure line, a trained solution is in part a property of the regime that trained it. Proposed: the deep-learning evidence is one network, under assumptions the paper concedes are strained. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-210](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-210.md) v2 | Init and optimizer set position on symmetry orbits | Zhao, Walters & Yu (2025), [LIT-970](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-970.md), read in [NOTE-712](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-712.md): a survey, so the dynamical results are secondhand. Continuous parameter-space symmetries (GL, scaling, orthogonal, translation) make minima positive-dimensional and connected, which is one source of mode connectivity. Under gradient flow each gives a conserved quantity, such as layer imbalance, that is fixed by initialization and locates the endpoint on the manifold. Under SGD these are not conserved. Read first-hand (Neural Mechanics; Ziyin et al.), weight decay drives the conserved quantities toward zero, and minibatch noise drives a rescaling symmetry's toward the point where the layers' gradient noise balances. The survey had reported this as imbalance decaying with large learning rates, and a stationary distribution biased toward balanced solutions that a Langevin model does not predict. This is the null-space half that [THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md)'s limiting dynamics leave out. Proposed: one survey, with the SGD results unread here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md) v5 | SGD noise equalizes noise across symmetric groups | Ziyin, Li & Ueda ([LIT-1012](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1012.md), read in [NOTE-714](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-714.md)), with the gradient flow conservation law and the Itô term from Neural Mechanics ([LIT-1013](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1013.md)). If ℓ(u, w) = ℓ(λu, w/λ) for every sample, then under the SDE model of SGD d(‖u‖² − ‖w‖²)/dt = −T(uᵀC₁u − wᵀC₂w), with T = η/S. The noise has no component along the symmetry, but its dependence on the parameters produces a deterministic drift through Itô's lemma. The drift points to the noise-balanced point, and weight decay adds to its rate. In a diagonal linear network the stationary distribution follows exactly: it is non-ergodic, has a memory of initialization, and collapses to zero above a critical temperature. The law is re-derived here (2026-10-19) within the SDE model; the tests are small synthetic networks, and whether it holds in deep networks on real data is QUESTION-164. | Active |
| [THEORY-212](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-212.md) v3 | Layer balance sets rich versus lazy learning | Dominé et al. (2025), [LIT-943](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-943.md), read in [NOTE-715](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-715.md). With whitened inputs and a λ-balanced start, W₂ᵀW₂ − W₁W₁ᵀ = λI, the full gradient flow is solved exactly. λ is conserved and sets the regime. As λ → 0, singular values are learned in sigmoidal stages, as in Saxe et al., and both layers become task-specific. As \|λ\| → ∞, learning is exponential, the NTK is static, and the larger layer stays near the identity while the smaller carries the task at scale ∝ 1/\|λ\|. The paper analyses gradient flow only. Under SGD the conserved quantity drifts ([THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md)), which [QUESTION-081](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-081.md) takes up. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-213](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-213.md) v4 | Weight decay puts minima on mirror subspaces | Ziyin (2024), [LIT-1014](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1014.md), read in [NOTE-716](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-716.md). If a per-sample loss is invariant under the reflection I − 2OOᵀ, then Oᵀθ = 0 is a stationary condition for GD and SGD. The Hessian is block diagonal there. Above a critical weight decay all minima satisfy the constraint. Under SGD with strong noise the subspace is attractive even at a strict saddle, by a Lyapunov-exponent argument. Rescaling, rotation and permutation symmetries imply mirrors, so they yield sparsity, low rank and merged neurons, with collapse and loss of plasticity as consequences. The SGD half is approximate and the network evidence is limited; the title holds only the exact half. Promoted on 2026-10-20 on the exact half, re-derived. The SGD half is QUESTION-206. | Active |
| [THEORY-246](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-246.md) v3 | Class separation hurts linear transfer | Kornblith, Chen, Lee & Norouzi (2021), [LIT-1044](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1044.md), read in [NOTE-762](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-762.md). Across nine objectives for ResNet-50 on ImageNet, penultimate class separation R² runs from 0.349 (softmax) to 0.845 (squared error), Papyan's Tr(Σ_W Σ_B†)/C from 21.2 to 0.33, and mean linear transfer to eight new-class datasets falls with R² (Spearman ρ = −0.93), from 75.9% to 48.3%. Cosine-softmax temperature raises R² from 0.24 to 0.77 and lowers transfer from 76.0% to 58.9%. CKA puts the differences in the last third of the network; fine-tuning erases them. The cost is for new classes: relearning the training classes, more separation helps. Networks early-stopped near 92% training accuracy; one dataset; correlational across losses. Promoted 2026-10-20 on this one study (ADR-047 v3), narrowed to what it measured. | Active |
| [THEORY-331](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-331.md) | High inference volume shifts compute up front | Sardana et al. (2024; arXiv 2023), [LIT-1070](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1070.md), read in [NOTE-881](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-881.md), and Snell et al. (2024), [LIT-1063](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1063.md), read in [NOTE-869](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-869.md). Sardana et al. minimise training plus lifetime inference FLOPs at a fixed loss under a Chinchilla-fitted law: the optimum moves to smaller models trained longer as known demand grows (28% fewer FLOPs at 30B quality and 10^13 inference tokens), and 47 runs show loss still falling at extreme ratios but more slowly than the law predicts. Snell et al. match FLOPs between a small model with test-time search or revision and a ~14× larger model on MATH: test-time compute wins at a low ratio of inference to pretraining tokens on easier questions and loses at a high ratio, and on the hardest at every ratio. Both take expected use as a known aggregate; neither has staleness or uncertainty about demand, and Snell's evidence is one model family on 500 questions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-342](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-342.md) v3 | Training and search compute trade log-linearly | Jones (2021), [LIT-1069](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1069.md), read in [NOTE-884](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-884.md). Across about 200 AlphaZero models on Hex boards 3×3 to 9×9, the best Elo for a given training compute follows one change-point curve, shifted by a fixed factor of compute per board row. On 9×9 only, iso-Elo contours of training against test-time search compute are straight in log–log space (fit: log test = −1.2·log train + 0.004·Elo + 29) over roughly 1e14–1e16 FLOPS-seconds of training, ending at a one-node search. One game, one nonstandard implementation, no uncertainty on the fitted coefficients, and no count of how many searches the trained agent will run, so it gives an exchange rate, not an amortization. | Active |
| [THEORY-421](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-421.md) v3 | Hyperbolic radius only partly reads hierarchy | Yang, Zhou, Ying, Chen & King (2023), [LIT-871](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-871.md), read in [NOTE-669](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-669.md). On two synthetic 3-ary trees of eight levels, HGCN leaves the root at hyperbolic distance 1.8–3.3 from the origin where the minimum is 1.2–2.4, the distances are roughly normal rather than leaf-heavy, and radius orders true levels for 69–75% of 5,000 random pairs. Recentring on the centroid plus an outward push raises that to 75–84%. The diagnosis rests on one architecture, two synthetic trees and one table without variance, and the paper does not separate a real failure to order levels from the origin's arbitrariness under losses that see only pairwise distances. | Active |
| [THEORY-425](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-425.md) v3 | Clean-data mode paths shed backdoors | Zhao, Chen, Das, Ramamurthy & Lin (2020), [LIT-668](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-668.md), read in [NOTE-530](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-530.md). A quadratic Bezier path trained on 50–2,500 clean samples between two backdoored VGG-16s on CIFAR-10 has, at t = 0.1, 88% clean accuracy and 1.1% backdoor success with 2,500 samples, and 63% and 2.5% with 50; injected weight errors fail at every point of such paths. Paths trained with the standard loss between regular and adversarially trained models are flat in standard loss with a PGD-loss barrier correlated with the input Hessian's top eigenvalue (0.71–0.88). The proposition offered for that correlation rests on an assumption that would remove the barrier. | Active |
| [THEORY-481](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-481.md) v4 | Linear attention learns staged by input spectrum | Mainali & Teixeira (2025), [LIT-859](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-859.md), read in [NOTE-658](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-658.md). The prediction of one linear-attention layer reduces to p₂ W Σ̂_x q₁ x_q, a product of two learned factors, so averaged gradient flow decouples into modes with τ_α dp_α/dt = q_α(1 − p_α q_α s^∞_α) and τ_α = (ηP s_α²)⁻¹, logistic from a balanced start. The fixed point is ŷ = W Σ̂_x Σ_x⁻¹ x_q as N → ∞. The paper's finite-N form, the one Ahn et al. and Zhang, Frei & Bartlett found, holds at finite N only for isotropic inputs with equal modes. The trajectory is new. The decoupling into independent modes is exact as N → ∞. At finite N it holds only for isotropic inputs with equal modes: the paper commutes the non-diagonal empirical covariance at (A71) and (A73), and the correct Wishart moment couples the modes at order 1/N. Alignment of the weights with the data's eigenbasis is assumed throughout, the null blocks vanish only in expectation over tasks, and the transfer to non-linear transformers is timing coincidences. | Active |
| [THEORY-496](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-496.md) v2 | Demo label correctness barely matters in ICL | Min et al. (2022), [LIT-814](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-814.md), read in [NOTE-607](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-607.md). With k = 16 demonstrations, labels drawn at random from the correct label set cost 0–5 points against gold labels (2.6 on classification, 1.7 on multiple choice on average) across twelve model–inference combinations and 26 datasets. Out-of-distribution inputs, random English words as labels, or breaking the input–label pairing each cost far more. The random labels always come from the right label set, gaps reach about 14 points on single datasets, and the authors' reading that the models learn no new correspondence at test time is untested on tasks pretraining cannot have taught. | Active |
| [THEORY-504](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-504.md) v3 | SAE fidelity measures disagree by site | Lieberum et al. (2024), [LIT-611](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-611.md), read in [NOTE-482](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-482.md). Across every layer and sublayer of Gemma 2 2B and 9B, JumpReLU autoencoders on the residual stream raise the language model's loss more, when spliced in, than MLP and attention autoencoders whose FVU is about the same; and autoencoders trained on the base model lose little loss on instruction-tuned rollouts while showing a larger FVU gap. The authors' explanations (the residual stream is the bottleneck; fine-tuning re-weights old features) are conjectures, and the authors say no agreed metric of autoencoder quality exists. | Active |
| [THEORY-509](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-509.md) | MoE gate symmetry is only expert permutation | Tran, Trinh, Bui & Nguyen (2025), [LIT-670](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-670.md), read in [NOTE-513](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-513.md). Softmax is invariant to a common shift of scores and the sum to the order of terms, so G(n) = ℝ^d × ℝ × S_n preserves the layer; Theorems 4.1–4.2 show that generically it is all of the gate's symmetry, for dense gating and for top-k with k ≥ 2 (top-1 has an extra scaling). Aligning expert order and then each expert's hidden units gives barriers of 0.0044–0.0066 between GPT-2 MoE layers fine-tuned from different seeds, against 0.14–0.86 without the order step. Every experiment shares and freezes the backbone around the inserted layer, so it is not evidence about independently trained MoE models. | Active |
| [THEORY-510](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-510.md) | Crop tolerance varies by class; some classes lose | Balestriero, Bottou & LeCun (2022), [LIT-234](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-234.md), read in [NOTE-845](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-845.md). Six pretrained models on cropped test images keep some classes recognisable at an 8% crop and lose others below about 50%, and agree on which. Over 20 ResNet-50 runs, moving the crop lower bound from 100% to 8% raises mean accuracy from about 70% to 76% while "academic gown" falls from about 62% to 40%. The classes shown are hand-picked; the per-class test rejects for 4.4% of classes at the 5% level, uncorrected for 1,000 tests, which alone is not more than chance; and evaluation-set noise is not counted. Theorem 1 does not reach which classes pay. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-521](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-521.md) | Generalization error can jump at critical load | Martin & Mahoney (2017), [LIT-672](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-672.md), read in [NOTE-542](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-542.md), restating Seung, Sompolinsky & Tishby (1992) and Haussler, Kearns, Seung & Tishby (1996), which the record does not hold. Generalization is set by maximizing s(ε) − α ln(1/(1 − ε)). For weights on a sphere s(ε) ~ ln ε and ε ~ 1/α; for ±1 weights s(ε) ~ −(π²/2)ε² ln ε, the first-order condition has no solution past a critical load, and the error drops to zero. Uniform bounds that see a class only through its size or VC dimension are smooth and blind to this. That deep networks have such a phase diagram is the authors' conjecture, and their mapping of label noise to load and early stopping to temperature is an analogy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-557](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-557.md) | Mode connectivity holds beyond image classifiers | Li et al. (2025), [LIT-676](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-676.md), read in [NOTE-529](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-529.md): GCN node classifiers from different seeds, on 12 real graphs and synthetic CSBM graphs, show linear barriers that a fitted quadratic Bezier curve removes. Yao, Zhang & Tian (2026), [LIT-660](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-660.md), read in [NOTE-534](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-534.md): one pair of DDPMs and one pair of small CLIP models joined by chains of checkpoints whose training loss stays under a threshold, where AutoNEB's paths rise steeply on CLIP. The evidence is plots without barrier numbers in the first, one pair per model and retrained anchors in the second. Zhang & Blei's claim of flat paths between LDA's ELBO maxima ([LIT-677](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-677.md)) reports no results. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-566](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-566.md) v3 | Hyperbolic nets curve only through biases | Ganea, Bécigneul & Hofmann (2018), [LIT-879](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-879.md), read in [NOTE-686](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-686.md), which checked the closed forms numerically. Möbius layers are defined as exp₀ ∘ f ∘ log₀, so any composition of them is exp₀ ∘ (the Euclidean composition) ∘ log₀, as the paper notes; only the Möbius bias, which is parallel transport from the origin followed by the exponential map, and the hyperbolic logistic regression's distances to geodesic hyperplanes are not absorbed by the chart. The structural fact is proved; that the networks' gains, confined to a synthetic task and to separating WordNet subtrees in low-dimensional Poincaré embeddings, come from those two operations is this record's inference. [NOTE-686](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-686.md) filed no THEORY. | Active |
| [THEORY-578](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-578.md) | Fisher–Rao geodesics can be low-loss paths | Tan, Long, Zhao & Laine (2023), [LIT-662](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-662.md), read in [NOTE-521](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-521.md). Two ResNet-20s at 4× width with LayerNorm, CIFAR-10, permuted by Git Re-Basin's weight matching: the straight line between them still has a large loss barrier, and a chain of 25 models optimised from it to minimise Σ JSD between neighbours on unlabelled training images keeps train and test loss low. One pair, one figure, no numbers in the text. The hypothesis that every geodesic between SGD solutions is mode-connecting is stated, not tested, and a chain whose neighbours agree in output may be low-loss almost by construction. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-675](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-675.md) | Linear barriers depend on data structure | Li et al. (2025), [LIT-676](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-676.md), read in [NOTE-529](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-529.md): on synthetic CSBM graphs the barrier between GCNs from different seeds falls with density and feature separability and peaks at middling homophily; GCN, GraphSAGE and GAT barriers are similar, an MLP's differ. Zhou, Zhang & Tsang (2023), [LIT-666](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-666.md), read in [NOTE-517](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-517.md): FedAvg global models from one random start under more heterogeneous clients are separated by a larger line barrier, joined by a one-bend chain, and the barrier falls with width. Both readings named this account and held it back. The GNN proofs are missing and its barriers are plots; the federated bound treats heterogeneity as isotropic noise, and its lemma and theorem conditions conflict as written. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-683](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-683.md) | Example order swings few-shot accuracy widely | Lu et al. (2021, ACL 2022), [LIT-833](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-833.md), read in [NOTE-626](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-626.md). All 24 orders of four balanced SST-2 examples give accuracies from about 50% to above 85%, in GPT-2 and GPT-3 models of eight sizes; Spearman correlations of order accuracy between sizes lie between −0.35 and 0.27 (175B against 2.7B: 0.05). The variance stays high up to 32 examples and after calibration. It is a measurement on causal GPT models and text classification, with the transfer analysis resting on one example set, and the paper finds no property of an order that predicts its effect. | Active |
| [THEORY-718](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-718.md) | Evidence is likelihood times an Occam factor | MacKay (1992), [LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md), Eqs. 5–6 with Eqs. 16 and 19–20, read in [NOTE-471](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-471.md): for y = Φw + noise with Gaussian noise of precision β and the prior w ~ N(0, α⁻¹I) on k weights, the posterior is exactly Gaussian, so the evidence is exactly P(D\|w_MP) times the Occam factor P(w_MP)(2π)^{k/2} det^{-1/2}A, with A = αI + βΦᵀΦ. If ΦᵀΦ/n converges to a positive-definite matrix and w_MP stays bounded, the log Occam factor is −(k/2) log n + O(1). Exact for this model class only. The general regular case and the singular case are [THEORY-087](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md), which is Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-736](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-736.md) v2 | Dropout-stable solutions are mode connected | Kuditipudi et al. (2019), [LIT-671](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-671.md), Theorem 1, read in full in [NOTE-544](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-544.md), with Draxler et al.'s (2018) concatenation bound from [LIT-653](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-653.md). Dropout stability gives every solution a half-width copy with the same loss up to ε. Half the units are then free, so working units can be swapped in and permuted at no cost. That joins any two such solutions. It is a statement about dropout-stable solutions only: whether training produces them is [THEORY-109](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-109.md)'s open question, and Theorem 4 of the same paper builds disconnected global minima. | Active |
| [THEORY-741](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-741.md) | Wide nets' global minima share a linked minimum | Lin, Li and Wu (2024), [LIT-682](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-682.md), Theorems 6, 11 and 18 with Lemmas 7 and 25, read in [NOTE-535](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-535.md) and re-derived by the promotion audit. Two toy models whose minima can be written down: a two-layer ReLU student of an orthonormal teacher on the sphere at population loss, and a deep linear network fitting y = Qx. Spare width lets every minimum be moved, along segments of minima, to one a common centre can reach. No permutation symmetry is used, and nothing is claimed about trained networks. | Active |
| [THEORY-779](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-779.md) v2 | Momentum SGD's stationary spread follows Hessian | Kunin et al. (2021), [LIT-1011](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1011.md), §§4–6 and App. G, read in [NOTE-711](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-711.md); the stationary moments re-derived by the promotion audit. An exact result for a model: Σ ∝ H constant and a quadratic loss are assumptions, and nothing here says a deep network meets them. The probability current is nonzero but reversible: under the model's assumptions the stationary process is time-reversible once velocities are flipped, so it is "broken detailed balance" only in the paper's sense, a nonzero current. | Active |
| [THEORY-781](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-781.md) | Strong SGD noise makes symmetric subspaces attract | Ziyin (2024), [LIT-1014](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1014.md), read in [NOTE-716](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-716.md). Beyond the exact half that [THEORY-213](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-213.md) holds, the paper argues by a Lyapunov-exponent analysis that strong SGD noise makes a mirror's subspace attracting even at a strict saddle, and reads sparsity, low rank and identical neurons in trained networks as its result. That analysis rests on a second-order, diagonal- Hessian approximation, and the network evidence is a ResNet18's correlation blocks. The test is [QUESTION-206](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-206.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-782](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-782.md) | Grokking onset: pairs fix the representation | Liu, Kitouni, Nolte, Michaud, Tegmark and Williams (2022), [LIT-858](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-858.md), read in [NOTE-662](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-662.md), with Power et al.'s critical fraction ([LIT-341](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-341.md)). The paper presents the critical training fraction as where the training set's equations fix the embedding. [THEORY-181](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-181.md) holds the theorem for the ideal model and the match at the one size measured, p = 10 with 1D embeddings. Held to addition: for S₃ the networks generalise beyond this mechanism. The multi-size test is [QUESTION-199](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-199.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-788](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-788.md) | Training past zero error yields neural collapse | Papyan, Han and Donoho (2020), [LIT-618](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-618.md), title their paper on the "prevalence" of neural collapse and present it as a pervasive outcome of the terminal phase of training. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md), only what their runs measured: three architectures with cross-entropy on seven balanced datasets without augmentation. This is the general law, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-790](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-790.md) | SGD noise balances rescaling-symmetric groups | Ziyin, Li & Ueda, [LIT-1012](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1012.md), read in [NOTE-714](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-714.md), with the Itô term from [LIT-1013](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1013.md). The law of balance is proved in the SDE model of SGD, and that part is the Active [THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md). The authors present the law as general to networks with rescaling symmetry, but test it only on small synthetic networks. This THEORY holds the general claim, for deep networks on real data, which no measurement in the record yet supports. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-794](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-794.md) | Compositional generalization needs diverse combos | Uselis, Dittadi & Oh (2025), [LIT-667](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-667.md), read in [NOTE-525](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-525.md). Their title and abstract present diversity of combinations, not data volume, as what drives compositional generalization in vision models. Their evidence is ResNet-50s trained from scratch on two-concept grids, with checkpoints chosen on the unseen pairs, and that measured part, with the factorization theorem, is the Active [THEORY-117](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-117.md). This THEORY holds the general causal claim. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-798](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-798.md) | Encoders differ by an angle-preserving map | Moschella, Maiorca, Fumero, Norelli, Locatello & Rodolà (2022; ICLR 2023), [LIT-849](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-849.md), read in [NOTE-652](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-652.md). The hypothesis behind relative representations, filed apart from what their experiments measured ([THEORY-175](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-175.md)) under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. The source assumes it and tests it only through its consequences; it never fits a map between two spaces. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-825](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-825.md) | Hyperbolic embeddings don't put roots at origin | Yang, Zhou, Ying, Chen & King (2023), [LIT-871](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-871.md), read in [NOTE-669](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-669.md), assert for hyperbolic graph models in general what they measured for HGCN on two synthetic trees: the root is not innermost and radius reads level only partly. The general form was the lead clause of [THEORY-421](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-421.md) until that account was narrowed to the measurement on 2026-10-20 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4); it is filed here so that it stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-828](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-828.md) | Weight averaging moves fine-tunes inward | Gueta, Venezian, Raffel, Slonim, Katz and Choshen (2023), [LIT-658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-658.md), read in [NOTE-515](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-515.md), conclude that fine-tuning "typically" yields models on the boundary of a region whose centre is better, and read model soups and SWA as picking points inside it (§§8–9). The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-105](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-105.md), only the probe-loss comparisons of hull points with members and the BitFit result, for RoBERTa-base on English classification. This is their geometric thesis, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-1353](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1353.md) | Circuits form when last parts align at once | Dong (2026), read in [NOTE-1540](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1540.md). One rate equation, sites × attempts × drive × e^(−βK) minus destruction, with K the missing parts. Forward, a capability ignites above a data-concentration floor that is a saddle–node; backward, plasticity loss is site depletion, silent in the loss and repaired by a query–key reset; and no native SGD knob is a temperature. Evidence: a toy grid, ablation on Pythia (32 of 32 cells below partial credit, 22 of 32 on the preregistered criterion) and six seeds for the reset. Proposed: single-author, unreplicated, mixing unproved. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1386](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1386.md) | Neural net inverse-designs Kresling energy curves | Kang, Kim, Yang and Ryu (2025), [LIT-2086](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2086.md), read in [NOTE-1619](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1619.md). Forward and inverse results are checked against a beam-truss FEA that shares the network's truss abstraction; the folding order is checked also in one scaled PET prototype, where barriers differ from prediction and are compared after normalizing to the bottom layer. It does not say the truss model captures the mechanics of real cells. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1651](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1651.md) | Up to 17% of ML reviews were LLM-modified | Liang et al. (2024), Monitoring AI-Modified Content at Scale: A Case Study on the Impact of ChatGPT on AI Conference Peer Reviews, read in [NOTE-1757](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1757.md) (Skimmed). The authors estimate, at corpus level, the fraction α of text substantially modified or generated by an LLM, by maximum likelihood over word-frequency distributions estimated from human-written and AI-generated reference corpora, validated on semi-synthetic mixtures. Applied to peer reviews, α rose sharply after ChatGPT's release at ML conferences (ICLR 1.6% to 10.6%; NeurIPS 1.9% to 9.1%; CoRL 2.4% to 6.5%; EMNLP about 16.9%) but not in Nature-portfolio reviews. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1672](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1672.md) | Agentic RL helps only with ample turn budgets | What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents? (Zhu, Jin, Tu, Men, Hao, Li, Liu, Zhao 2026), read in [NOTE-1769](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1769.md) (Read). The paper asks what multi-turn agentic RL (GRPO mainly, also PPO and GiGPO, on Qwen3-4B/8B) improves over its base model, on four interactive benchmarks (DeepCoder-MT, BFCL v3, InterCode-SQL, FrozenLake), using the two-dimensional metric Pass@(K, T) of Zhai et al. (2026; arXiv 2604.14877, held as [LIT-2441](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2441.md)). Across sampling breadth K, the RL model beats the base model at every k, so in multi-turn settings RL pushes success beyond the base model's empirical Pass@K boundary (unlike single-turn results). | Proposed |

| [THEORY-1826](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1826.md) | Edit condition-number growth degrades models | Ma, Wang, Xu, Ling & Gu (2025), [LIT-2552](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2552.md), read in [NOTE-1910](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1910.md). The causal reading rests on a perturbation upper bound for a proxy quantity, on the rise of the condition number with edits, and on a correlation between that rise and the decline (C.5). The remedy's benefit is shown on three editors and three LLMs. The sharp edges: there is no intervention on the condition number at fixed update size; the bound's side conditions are not checked; and PRUNE does not provably bound the condition number. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1827](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1827.md) v2 | Linear guardedness iff class means are equal | Belrose, Schneider-Joseph, Ravfogel, Cotterell, Raff & Biderman (2023), [LIT-2551](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2551.md), read in [NOTE-1912](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1912.md). Theorems in population moments, and exact for the moments fitted. The sharp edges: the guarantee is linear only, and the authors conjecture that nonlinear erasure without damage is intractable in general; there is no finite-sample bound; and the oblique eraser can enlarge norms. | Active |
| [THEORY-1828](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1828.md) | Null-space misalignment breaks multi-domain edits | Liang, Lin, Huang, Wu, Li, Wang & Yan (2026), [LIT-2554](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2554.md), read in [NOTE-1911](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1911.md). The intersection bound is elementary linear algebra and holds; the claim that misalignment explains the collapse rests on results from one editor family, five to seven domains and three backbones, with conflict used as a surrogate for forgetting. The sharp edges: the Conflict Index is degenerate as defined at the paper's own sizes unless null spaces are thresholded, and the threshold is not given; and in the seven-task test, ordering by conflict does no better than the average random order, which weakens the link from measured conflict to forgetting. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1829](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1829.md) | Null-space projection sustains sequential edits | Fang, Jiang, Wang, Ma, Shi, Wang, He & Chua (2025), [LIT-2555](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2555.md), read in [NOTE-1908](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1908.md). Exact preservation holds for an exact null space; the method uses a thresholded one, so preservation is approximate and its size unmeasured. The sequential-editing results are strong on LLaMA3 and hold on GPT-J and GPT2-XL. The sharp edges: no measurement of leakage, no reported null-space dimension, specificity well below pre-edit, and a misstated "best baseline" comparison. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1832](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1832.md) | KV cache reuse erodes multi-turn steering | Kang, Liu, Ma, Huang, Tan & Jiang (2026), [LIT-2549](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2549.md), read in [NOTE-1905](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1905.md). The cache account rests on a 2×2 isolation test on one model and 7 traits, with intervals. The method's advantage rests on point estimates from one judge and one seed on Qwen2.5-7B, with a Llama replication and judge checks on 4 traits. The sharp edges: injection itself, not the cache, is the larger cause of lost coherence; cleaning the cache does not reduce pooled drift; and the title's "duality" is not a result. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1854](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1854.md) | AI devices rest on planetary extraction | Crawford and Joler (2018), read in [NOTE-1917](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1917.md). AI as extraction; transparency not enough. A stand-in for [LIT-2593](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2593.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1872](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1872.md) | Low-frequency update gaps hurt merging | Zheng & Wang (2025), [LIT-2643](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2643.md), read in [NOTE-1974](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1974.md). Amplitude variance across tasks is largest at low index-grid frequencies and correlates negatively with normalized merged accuracy; FR-Merging (high-pass then magnitude-weighted sum) reaches 78.1 on ViT-B/32 with 8 tasks against 70.1 for task arithmetic and 73.6 for TIES. The frequencies are over the arbitrary order of rows and columns and change under a function-preserving permutation of hidden units, which the paper does not test. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
